source.title: Interpreting Large Text-to-Image Diffusion Models with Dictionary Learning
source.authors: Stepan Shabalin; Ayush Panda; Dmitrii Kharlapenko; A. Ali; Yixiong Hao; Arthur Conmy

record.tranche_reason: The study applies SAEs and ITDA as tools for interpreting diffusion-model activations and compares their explanation scores with MLP neurons. It does not measure whether neurons respond to unrelated inputs.
record.gate_note: The study scores explanations of maximum-activating examples, but does not test whether a neuron responds to several unrelated inputs or whether such inputs share a feature. The reported interpretability-score comparison is recorded as a related finding under fits_no_version. Cited results from other studies and the paper's steering examples are not results about polysemanticity.
record.test_reason: The study trains SAEs and ITDA on FLUX.1 and scores explanation accuracy of max-activating examples against an MLP-neuron baseline. It does not measure whether neurons respond to unrelated inputs, their share, causes, or dependence on architecture or measurement. The lower neuron autointerp score is a related but different construct (explanation accuracy), so it goes under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct as paraphrased. Additionally, the authors note that ITDA features encode general attributes (colours, textures) while SAE features capture concrete objects. They also find SAE steering effective but limited to prompts related to the feature.
record.recipe_differences: The study applies dictionary learning and visual automated interpretation to a text-to-image diffusion model, rather than testing mixed responses in image-classifier neurons. It uses maximum-activating examples and an explanation-scoring pipeline.

fits_no_version.finding: In FLUX.1 double block 18, MLP neurons score lower on visual autointerp accuracy (mean 0.654) than SAE (0.819) and ITDA (0.776) features. Some neurons score very high.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In a large text-to-image diffusion transformer, MLP neurons are on average less accurately explained from max-activating examples than sparse dictionary features.

record.problems: The study does not directly test polysemanticity. Its neuron comparison uses maximum-activating examples and an automated explanation score; the authors themselves note possible pipeline bias, including sensitivity to simple image characteristics such as color. No uncertainty estimates for the plotted scores are stated.
record.rows_left_out: No results bearing on the claim were left out. Reconstruction and steering results do not measure polysemanticity.

untested.parts: Neurons in image classifiers responding to unrelated inputs; FLUX.1 is a diffusion transformer, and no mixed-response rate is measured.
Share of language-model MLP neurons responding to unrelated tokens, and its layer dependence.
Superposition as a cause. Superposition is only cited as motivation for SAEs.
Effects of activation function, architecture or regularization on the neuron polysemantic share, and performance cost.
Whether apparent mixtures share one feature.
Dependence of polysemanticity on activation range or scoring method. Only max-activating examples and one scorer are used, and this choice is not varied.

record.verdict_notes: The neuron baseline is an interpretability-score comparison only. The paper never classifies neurons as polysemantic or monosemantic, and it does not examine whether low-scoring neurons respond to unrelated concepts. It is not an original source. Steering and reconstruction results are irrelevant to the claim.

versions.untested_parts: Whether vision-model neurons respond strongly to several unrelated kinds of input.
Language-model neurons and unrelated tokens or contexts.
Whether polysemanticity is caused by superposition or capacity pressure.
Polysemanticity without capacity pressure, including effects of initialization, regularization, or training noise.
Changes in polysemanticity across architectures, activation functions, or regularization, and any performance cost.
Whether apparently mixed neuron responses share a feature or related job.
Whether polysemanticity judgments change with activation range or explanation-scoring method.

rows.subject: FLUX.1 MLP neurons
rows.operation_detail: Scored explanations of maximum-activating examples with the visual autointerpretation pipeline.
rows.measure: AutoInterp accuracy score; mean and median
rows.note: The paper states that MLP neurons are generally less interpretable than SAE and ITDA features, while noting that some MLP neurons have very high scores. This score does not measure unrelated response types.
rows.check: Explanation-accuracy score on max-activating examples, not a polysemanticity rate. Values are figure labels (mean 0.654, median 0.650), with no baseline or uncertainty. Subject is MLP neurons in a diffusion transformer, not an image classifier or language model.

rows.subject: FLUX.1 SAE features
rows.operation_detail: Scored explanations of maximum-activating examples with the visual autointerpretation pipeline.
rows.measure: AutoInterp accuracy score; mean and median
rows.note: The paper reports that SAE and ITDA scores are comparable, and that SAE features score above MLP neurons generally. This is an explanation-accuracy result, not a measure of polysemanticity.
rows.check: The study's own method (SAE features) compared as an alternative to neurons. It is not a measure of neuron polysemanticity, so it should be a comparator only.

rows.subject: FLUX.1 ITDA features
rows.operation_detail: Scored explanations of maximum-activating examples with the visual autointerpretation pipeline.
rows.measure: AutoInterp accuracy score; mean and median
rows.note: The paper reports scores comparable to SAE features and generally above MLP neurons. This score does not measure unrelated response types.
rows.check: The study's own method (ITDA features), a comparator only. It does not measure neuron polysemanticity.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
